subject: Post-demo follow-up: BlueGrid evaluation — streaming & tool-calling probe
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@bluegrid.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: BlueGrid evaluation — streaming & tool-calling probe

Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum going.

Highlights from the demo
- Streaming: showed low-latency token streaming with client-side reconnects and partial JSON assembly. We measured median tail latency ~35ms/token in the demo environment.
- Tool/Function calling: demonstrated synchronous tool invocation + structured output enforcement via schema (json-schema enforcement).
- Observability: per-token cost breakdown and traceable request -> model variant routing.

BlueGrid asks we captured
- Side-by-side latency comparison with your current hyperscaler endpoint (streaming + non-streaming; 256-token windows).
- A parity check for function-calling (your router + Redwood calling an internal tool) to validate call semantics and retries.
- Proof that structured outputs (strict JSON objects) are produced reliably for our webhook consumer.
- Security/compliance detail for data residency and audit logs (I looped security later in thread).

Proposed probe plan (lightweight, 2-week):
1) Test artifacts for you: streaming-latency-test-plan.md (attached) and a small harness we can run against your staging endpoint. Owner: Ben Carter.
2) Side-by-side runs: same prompts + workload generator against BlueGrid hyperscaler endpoint and Redwood hosted endpoint. Measure: median, p95 per-token latency, end-to-end time, streaming reconnect behavior. Owner: Priyom Das.
3) Function-calling parity: we'll run 50 scripted calls that exercise nested tool chains and verify idempotency/retries and response schema enforcement. Owner: Marissa Cole.
4) Deliverable: short results deck + probe matrix (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-probe-matrix.xlsx attached). Deadline: initial results in 10 business days (5 May 2026).

Action items for BlueGrid
- Share a staging endpoint and test credentials (read-only) for the benchmark harness.
- Point of contact for security questions (audit logs / retention).
- Any prompt sets you want us to include (otherwise we'll synthesize based on the demo).

I'll kick off the harness and schedule a 30-min sync for the halfway checkpoint once we have the endpoint. If that works, I'll send calendar invites to the ones cc'd.

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: streaming-latency-test-plan.md (text/markdown)]
[Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-probe-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@bluegrid.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: BlueGrid Security <security@bluegrid.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@bluegrid.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: BlueGrid evaluation — streaming & tool-calling probe

Olga — appreciate the thorough recap and the artifacts. Quick answers and a couple of clarifying questions: 

1) Staging endpoint: we'll provision a short-lived key for your harness by EOD today. I'll send creds to the address in a separate email (security will need to approve the IP allowlist).
2) Prompts: please include both the 1) customer support triage prompts we demoed and 2) the content-generation prompts (long-form, ~400 tokens) so we can see behavior across sizes.
3) Security: looping in our security lead (security@bluegrid.com) for the audit log questions — they prefer artifact examples (schema for logs).

One ask on measurement: can you include streaming partiality metrics — i.e., how often the SDK resumes mid-stream after a transient, and whether tokens are replayed/duplicated? We saw a behavior previously where small reconnects caused repeated tokens.

We like the 10-business-day cadence. Tentatively, hold 4 May 2026 at 16:00 EDT for the midway check.

Thanks —
Alex
Alex Rivera
Director of Platform Engineering, BlueGrid Inc.

Quick internal note — I started the harness repo and wired the streaming test harness to our staging cluster. Short checklist:
- Harness can target arbitrary endpoints and will record per-token timestamps + stream session IDs.
- We'll produce a CSV with token timestamps, session_id, reconnect_count, duplicate_token_flag.
- Ben: please add the ip whitelist ranges to the test plan so BlueGrid can pre-approve.
- Marissa: for function-calling, I'll stub the BlueGrid webhook with a local simulator; we should capture call-id (traceable) and success/failure codes for each call.

I'll push an initial PR by EOD PST tomorrow (28 Apr).

— Priyom

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@bluegrid.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, BlueGrid Security <security@bluegrid.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: BlueGrid evaluation — streaming & tool-calling probe

Alex — great, thanks for the fast turnaround on creds and the prompt guidance. Two quick clarifications and the next calendar steps: 

1) Streaming partiality / duplicates: we will explicitly report duplicates per-session and include a dedup strategy recommendation using per-token sequence IDs and idempotency windows. If you'd like, we can also run a small mutational test that forces transient disconnects to quantify replay behavior.

2) Function-calling parity: Marissa will run the nested-call suite against your staging webhook simulator. We'll produce a short CSV of call_id, parent_call, result_hash, retry_count. That should map directly to your observability stack.

3) Security artifacts: BlueGrid Security, we'll send a short survey with our audit log schema and sample records after this note. Expect a separate email from security@redwood.ai.

4) Calendar: sending the 4 May halfway checkpoint invite now — 30 minutes to review interim numbers. Final deck delivery targeted 5 May by COB as agreed.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-probe-matrix.xlsx (probe matrix with metrics and owners)

Thanks all —
Olga
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
